title: FBI Interview of Timothy Leary on His 1970 Prison Escape and the Brotherhood of Eternal Love
author: Federal Bureau of Investigation
summary: An FBI FD-302 interview (July 1974) in which recaptured Timothy Leary decodes the coded correspondence from his September 1970 prison escape. Leary identifies the Brotherhood of Eternal Love as the Laguna Beach LSD collective 'Group', Michael Randall as 'M', attorney Michael Kennedy, fellow inmate William Bellinger, and the Weathermen as 'Consultants' who staged the escape.
excerpt: LEARY furnished the following explanation of terms used in the aforementioned letters: ... M — MICHAEL RANDALL ... Consuitants — Weathermen ... Land Deed — Passport ... Planet — Prison ... Appeal / Hearing — Escape ... Brief — Escape Plan ... Group — Brotherhood of Eternal Love.
citation: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Los Angeles Field Office file no. 100-76342, "Timothy Francis Leary, Jr., aka, et al.," FD-302 report of interview, July 17, 1974 (transcribed July 28, 1974), and airtel, SAC Los Angeles to SAC Chicago, August 12, 1974, in Timothy Leary FBI file (FOIA release), FBI Records: The Vault.
rights: US Government work (FBI investigative file released under the Freedom of Information Act). Public domain.

draft.rationale: A FOIA-released FBI investigative file is a US Government work and public domain, hostable in full; this FD-302 has Leary himself decoding the coded correspondence behind his 1970 prison escape, naming Michael Randall and the Brotherhood of Eternal Love (the Laguna Beach LSD-distribution collective) as the network that financed and helped stage it. Surveillance-record material of a kind the archive otherwise has nothing like.

textSource.scope: FD-302 interview of Leary (17 July 1974, transcribed 28 July 1974) and the transmittal airtel that follows it in the same Los Angeles field office file (100-76342), lines 3034-3742 of the full-file pdftotext -layout extraction. The surrounding ~500 pages of the file (surveillance material from the Harvard/Millbrook years through the mid-1970s) were downloaded and kept in raw/ for context but not transcribed.

textQuality.notes: vault.fbi.gov serves this as a 513-page, 27MB image-only PDF ('Timothy Francis Leary Part 01 of 01') that pdftotext -layout returns nothing for, as expected for a scanned document with no text layer. Internet Archive mirrors the same PDF (identifier TimothyLeary) with an OCR text layer already burned in as an 'Additional Text PDF'; pdftotext -layout on that derivative did yield substantial text, so the tesseract/pdftoppm fallback was not needed. Cross-checked a sample against IA's own djvu.txt derivative (same underlying OCR pass) and found the same readings. OCR quality on this heavily photocopied FOIA release is poor in places: confirmed misreadings include 'KENREDY' for KENNEDY, 'Brotherhood of Internal Love' for 'Brotherhood of Eternal Love' (item #45 in the report), 'Christmuas' for Christmas, 'regally ensconced' probably for 'legally ensconced' or similar, and the interviewing agent's name rendered 'R. J. IA JEUNZSSE, JR.' (almost certainly La Jeunesse). A short illegible routing-stamp/disclaimer block spanning a page break was cut and marked with an editorial note rather than transcribed. Bracketed redaction markers ([___]) are the OCR's rendering of the FBI's own black-bar redactions and vary in how cleanly they came through.
